The art ofbeing bored

Most of us never let ourselves get bored any more. There is always a phone within reach. For the next 90 minutes we’ll talk about what boredom feels like, what screens have done to it, and whether it might actually be good for us.

The art of being bored An exhibition in eight rooms for an online English speaking club, autumn 2026 Conversation, ten useful phrases and one minute of silence
Level
B1–C1
Length

Room1

Warm-up

Minutes 0 to 10

Easy questions to get us talking. Short answers are fine, and there are no wrong ones.

Warm-up questions

Unmute and answer in a sentence or two. Then pass the question on: say the name of the next person who answers.

This or that

Type A or B in the chat. Then unmute and explain your choice in one sentence. “Both” and “neither” are not allowed.

or
Room2

Words for doing nothing

Minutes 10 to 25

Ten phrases for the space between things. For each card, read the example aloud, then answer the question on the back.

Phrase roulette

You get a phrase and a topic. Talk for 45 seconds and use the phrase naturally. Everyone else listens for it and asks you one question at the end.

Room3

The gallery

Minutes 25 to 35

Six works on the theme of doing nothing. Pick one and describe it in three sentences, using at least two phrases from room 2.

The curator’s game

Describe one of the works without saying its title. The others write in the chat which one they think it is.

Then rename it. Every work here deserves a better title than the one on its label. Vote for the best new title in the chat.

Room4

Let’s talk

Minutes 35 to 55

Three rounds, from personal to the bigger picture. House rule: after every answer, someone else asks one follow-up question. Unmute and jump in.

Conversation toolkit

Steal these. Nobody will notice.

Buying time

That’s a good question, let me think… / It’s hard to say, but…

Agreeing

I couldn’t agree more. / That’s exactly how I feel.

Disagreeing politely

I see your point, but… / I’m not sure I’d go that far.

Asking for more

What do you mean by…? / Could you give an example? / How did that feel?

Linking to your life

That reminds me of… / Funnily enough, the same thing happened to me.

Room5

True or myth

Minutes 55 to 63

Read the statement and vote in the chat: T for true, M for myth. Then we reveal the answer. If the group is split, the minority gets 30 seconds to change everyone’s mind.

Group score: 0 of 0
Room6

Sixty seconds of nothing

Minutes 63 to 68

In 2014, researchers found that many people would rather give themselves a mild electric shock than sit alone with their thoughts. Let’s see how this group does with one minute.

Afterwards, talk about it

  • Did the minute feel long or short? Longer than you expected?
  • Where did your mind go first: the past, the future, or your to-do list?
  • Did you feel antsy? What did your hands want to do?
  • Would you do this every day? Be honest.

The rules: stay muted, hands off your keyboard and phone, no other tabs. You can turn your camera off. Look away from the screen, out of the window, or at nothing in particular.

Room7

Debate or clinic

Minutes 68 to 85

Two formats, two kinds of conversation. You’ll do one of them in breakout rooms.

The debate

This house believes that

  1. Two teams, for and against, each in its own breakout room.
  2. Three minutes to prepare your arguments.
  3. Back in the main room: one minute each for an opening statement.
  4. Five minutes of open debate. Raise your hand to speak.
  5. One minute each to sum up. Then everyone votes in the chat.
3:00
Useful phrasesThe main reason we believe this is… / Let me give you an example… / That may be true, but… / With all due respect, I’d argue that… / Let’s not forget that…

The boredom clinic

Today’s patient

  1. In a breakout room for two, one of you is the patient and the other is the doctor.
  2. The patient reads the card and describes the problem in their own words.
  3. The doctor asks at least three questions, then writes a prescription in the chat using two phrases from today.
  4. Swap roles and take a new patient.
For the doctorHow long have you been feeling…? / What usually happens when…? / Have you tried…? / My prescription is… / Try to… at least once a day.
Room8

Before you go

Minutes 85 to 90

Five minutes to close the exhibition. Everyone answers at least one question.

  • Which phrase from today will you actually use this week? Write a sentence with it in the chat.
  • Finish the sentence: “I used to think boredom was…, but now I think…”
  • What is one thing you’ll stop using to kill time?

This week’s challenge

Ten minutes of doing absolutely nothing, once a day. No phone, no music, no podcast. Next time, report back: was it restful, mind-numbing, or both?

Thank you for being bored with us.

The exhibition is now closed. Go and do nothing.
